body.text: This is your question for today. Keep it in mind during the games.
Three games tonight: standing, guarded, pinned. Win one and the next round gets harder. Lose it and you run the same one again.
Hand Fight to Closed Hand Connection via Underhook
Skill Learning Objective (SLO): Entering, for both players.
Both players stand facing each other, hand fighting range, both disconnected.
Connect to your partner's wrist, elbow, and head, get the underhook, and fight to a closed-hand connection around the head, body, or leg.

items: Whoever connects first wins. The same rule applies to both players.

body.text: SLO: Arriving for the top player, Leaving for the bottom player.
The bottom player is belly up in open guard. The top player is on his feet, starting by clearing the feet.

Top player: get one leg outside the bottom player's feet, make shin contact from knee to head, then without stopping go around to the other side and touch there too. Bottom player: hook and post with your feet to make the top player hit his butt, then sit up with your back off the mat.

items: The top player wins by touching one outside and then the other, one right after the other.
The bottom player wins by making the top player hit his butt and sitting up with his back off the mat.

body.text: SLO: Finishing for the top player, Leaving for the bottom player.
The top player is on the bottom player's back, hands connected, not yet in the finishing position. The bottom player may move freely.

Top player: first, get your over-grip palm to touch the bottom player's back. Once it touches, slide your wrist into the crook of your own other elbow and lock your hands. The win is the lock, not a squeeze. Bottom player: put your back on the mat, using any movement.

items: The top player wins by getting the palm to the back, then the wrist into the crook of his own other elbow with hands locked.
The bottom player wins when his back touches the mat.

slides.title: How you win it
slides.question: In Build to Rear Strangle Game, what wins it for the top player?

options.text: The top player wins by getting the palm to the back, then the wrist into the crook of his own other elbow with hands locked.
options.feedback: That is the win condition, and nothing else scores.

options.text: Holding the finish after your partner taps
options.feedback: Never. You let go the second your partner taps. Every single time. The tap is law.

options.text: Hurting your partner because you can
options.feedback: That is the one thing the Back Pin teaches you never to do. Total control, plus the choice not to hurt someone, is the heart of the whole program.

slides.correctText: That is how you win today.
